fits.ceiling: (i) fitted on every scored day with a spread, scored on the same days, at the ceiling settings: what any model could at best extract from these inputs; not a claim

reachable.reading: (ii) the same inputs, read at each row's own decision instant, refitted every 21 scored days at the reachable settings; a day with no fit (fewer than the minimum training rows) is not scored for any line
reachable.training_rows: the scored days whose spread row is at or before the last public row (the anchor) of the block's first decision instant; a row after it raises LookAheadError (training_positions)

hypothesis: H2 (docs/research/plan.md): the data we hold carries signal for the spread and for ordinary-day pressure; step 3, the upper bound

inputs.excluded: the six nowcast_* columns, which the as-of rule refuses as undeclared; #630's new sources (H3); nothing is chosen from a score
inputs.reading: derived_features_631.read_all's: the 'both' arm (announcement-dated settlements, per-release H.4.1) at the decision instant of lead h, each read checked by the as-of rule; a series not public at the lead is a hole, left missing

models.climatology: the training rate of the indicator (the in-sample rate for the ceiling)

gbm.spread: ml.grid_quantiles_gbm: HistGradientBoostingRegressor(loss='quantile') per level of the 23-level grid, sorted per day

models.persistence_logistic: ml.l2_logistic_probabilities on the last public spread alone, c = 1.0, the reachable fit's rule

ridge.indicator: ml.l2_logistic_probabilities on the same design, ordinary days only
ridge.spread: ml.ridge_location_scale_quantiles: ridge location and ridge absolute-residual scale on the standardised inputs (training mean imputed, clipped at +-5) and the products i <= j of the key columns; quantiles from the standardised training residuals

models.tuning: none: settings are fixed here; the ceiling's are looser (more rounds, more leaves, a weaker penalty) so that it is the more flexible fit

panel.built_by: docs/pivot/derived-features-result.md (Reproduce): the scratch panel DERIV.csv of #631

barely_above.indicator: the ordinary-day AUROC, averaged over leads 1 to 5, is under 0.6
barely_above.spread: the skill against B1 on ordinary days has a 90% stationary-bootstrap interval (5th to 95th percentile of the paired skill draws) whose lower end is at or below 0

reading_rule.benchmark_for_the_indicator: walk-forward climatology (the training rate) and a persistence-logistic model on the last public spread, reported; the line below is the issue's own absolute line
reading_rule.benchmark_for_the_spread: B1, as-of persistence (protocol v1 section 4); B2, calendar climatology, reported
reading_rule.effort_rule: H2 outcome rule (docs/research/hypotheses/H2.md): a data problem sends effort to H3 and H4, a model problem to H5's development steps
reading_rule.not_a_claim: the ceiling is fitted and scored in-sample, so it is an upper bound and not a forecast; a reachable figure is development evidence and gives no verdict (protocol v1 section 1)
reading_rule.source: the issue's text (#635, Eleonora, 12 October 2026), made operational here before any number; the scoring sections of the issue are superseded by protocol v1 (ruling on #635)

targets.primary: the spread in bp, 23-level grid CRPS averaged over leads 1 to 5 per decision day, on ordinary days (the target day is not a risk date)
targets.secondary: the +5 bp indicator on ordinary days, AUROC averaged over leads 1 to 5

reading_rule.the_verdict_line: stated for the spread (the primary target) and for the indicator, each under the rule; if they differ, both are stated and the primary target's decides the one-line verdict

verdict.data problem: the ceiling is barely above the benchmark
verdict.model problem: the ceiling is clearly above the benchmark and the reachable line is barely above it
verdict.partly reached: both are clearly above the benchmark; the gap between the ceiling and the reachable line is reported, with its paired interval

reading_rule.which_model: for each fit, the better of the two model families on the same days, by the point estimate of the quantity above; the choice is among two, on development data, and is reported as such

ruling: the scoring sections of #635 are superseded by scoring protocol v1 (docs/decisions/scoring-protocol.md, #640) wherever they differ: the metric (23-level grid CRPS over leads 1 to 5), the benchmarks (B1, B2) and the interval (stationary bootstrap, mean block 10); development days give no verdict

indicator.interval: the stationary bootstrap over the ordinary scored days in date order, mean block 10, 1000 draws, seed 635, one draw shared by every lead and model; the 90% interval is the 5th to 95th percentile
indicator.metrics: AUROC, and Brier skill against walk-forward climatology and against persistence-logistic, per lead and averaged over leads 1 to 5
indicator.splits: by regime and by as-of scarcity state (ample | scarce | unknown)

spread.benchmarks: protocol_benchmarks.b1_forecast and b2_forecast on the published panel cut at 2025-12-31
spread.interval: scoring_protocol.paired_tests: stationary bootstrap, mean block 10, seed 635, 10000 draws (2000 on the split tables); the 90% interval is the 5th to 95th percentile of the paired skill draws; the protocol's one-sided 95% lower bound of mean(d) is reported
spread.score: scoring_protocol.grid_crps, averaged over leads 1 to 5 per decision day (day_scores); MAE of the median beside it
spread.splits: all days, ordinary days, risk dates; by regime (metadata/evaluation_splits.json) on all and on ordinary days; by reporting day type; by lead; a split is reported, never a pass requirement

status: declared by the pull request that closes #635 before any score was computed; a development measurement (H2, step 3), never a claim or a verdict. Nothing is published, no variant joins a published declaration, no day after 2025-12-31 is read

targets.indicator: 1 if the spread is strictly above +5 bp on whole basis points (repo_model.data.exceeds_bp), on ordinary days: the risk-date rule of the model (announcement_dating_rescore.risk_flag with the coupon clause) is false
targets.spread: spread_bps at the scored day, in bp, first published, as a 23-level quantile law (scoring_protocol.GRID), led 1 to 5 business days

variant_count: four fitted families of two kinds (a quantile law and a classifier, each gradient-boosted and regularised linear), each at two settings (ceiling and reachable) and no other; no input list, setting or interaction was changed after a score
